name: Russia-Ukraine war (ground war)
summary: Europe's largest war since 1945 entered its fifth year with Russia still attacking along a roughly 1,200 km front but gaining almost nothing in 2026. Russia took Pokrovsk, Myrnohrad, Siversk and Huliaipole in late 2025, then stalled; Ukraine counterattacked in the south from February and north of Lyman from September. ISW assesses Russia has been net losing ground since 1 September 2026, while the battle for Kostiantynivka grinds on a year after it began.

sides.name: Ukraine
members: Armed Forces of Ukraine (Ground Forces army corps, Air Assault Forces, Marine Corps)
Military intelligence (HUR) and Security Service (SBU) special units
backers: European states (money, air defence, long-range missiles such as Storm Shadow; Germany delivered two Patriot systems in January 2026)
United States (intelligence sharing, Patriot interceptors and other weapons)
Canada (2 billion dollar package with 400+ armoured vehicles announced February 2026)
leaders: Kyrylo Budanov (Head of the Presidential Office from January 2026)
sides.strength: No reliable total found in this research. The drone branch was planned to grow sharply in 2026 and Ukrainian commanders consistently describe being outnumbered at the point of attack.

sides.name: Russia
members: Russian Armed Forces Groups of Forces: North, West, South, Center, East, Dnepr
Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia (formed 12 Nov 2025) incl. Rubikon Center and 50th 'Varyag' Brigade
Naval infantry and Airborne (VDV) formations used as fire brigades
backers: North Korea (troops in Russia's Kursk border region, about 12 million artillery shells by July 2025, Hwasong-11 ballistic missiles, labourers)
Belarus (territory, Oreshnik missiles placed on combat duty there on 30 Dec 2025)
leaders: Valery Gerasimov (Chief of the General Staff)
Yevgeny Nikiforov (Commander, Northern Group of Forces)
sides.strength: Recruitment about 940 per day against a target of 1,100 to 1,150 (Mick Ryan, June 2026). Russian drone forces estimated at 114,000 by Ukraine in May 2026. Losses exceeded intake for four straight months from December 2025.

background: Russia seized Crimea and parts of Donbas in 2014 and launched a full-scale invasion on 24 February 2022. After Ukraine's 2022 counteroffensives and the failed 2023 Ukrainian offensive, the war became an attritional struggle in which Russia traded very heavy casualties for slow gains in Donetsk Oblast. By September 2025 Russia occupied about 19% of Ukraine. The war matters because it is a test of whether borders can be changed by force in Europe, it pulls NATO states into a long contest of industrial output, and it has turned the battlefield into a laboratory for drone, electronic and missile warfare that every army now studies.
year: Late 2025 was Russia's last good stretch. Russian infiltration groups worked into Pokrovsk from October; Moscow claimed the city on 1 December 2025, and by 28 January 2026 Ukrainian troops were gone from both Pokrovsk and neighbouring Myrnohrad. Siversk fell in December (Ukraine confirmed on 23 December) and Huliaipole, a hub that had been quiet since 2022, was claimed on 27 December after a three-month push across the Yanchur and Haichur rivers. The exception was Kupiansk: Russia's generals claimed it in late 2025, but Ukrainian clearing operations left only a few dozen Russians holed up in one quarter by mid-February 2026. In February 2026 Starlink cut off unregistered terminals used by Russian units, degrading their command and control, and on 11 February Ukraine's Air Assault Forces opened a counteroffensive on the Oleksandrivka front where Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia oblasts meet. By 12 August Kyiv claimed 745 km2 and 26 villages, the largest Ukrainian gains since 2023, though Russia retook a few villages. Russia's spring offensive against the Donetsk 'fortress belt' of Sloviansk, Kramatorsk, Druzhkivka and Kostiantynivka opened in mid-March and achieved little: March 2026 was Russia's costliest month of the war at about 35,000 casualties. In Kostiantynivka Russian infiltrators reached the city centre and Moscow declared the city captured on 3 July, but Ukraine still holds positions there in late October. From mid-September Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps ran Operation Vivaldi against the Russian salient north of Lyman, retaking a string of villages and killing Moscow's plan to envelop the fortress belt from the northwest. Diplomacy produced talk but only short pauses: Berlin talks in December 2025 sketched a 'NATO-like' security guarantee, the first US-Ukraine-Russia trilateral talks met in Abu Dhabi on 23 and 24 January 2026 without agreements, the Kremlin agreed to Trump's request to halt strikes on Kyiv until 1 February, a 9 to 11 May Victory Day ceasefire that reduced but did not stop fighting, and a 72-hour Kyiv strike pause around the September Witkoff and Kushner visits.
situation: As of 27 October 2026 Russia is attacking on four axes around the Donetsk fortress belt without advancing: northeast and southeast of Lyman, east of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk (Russian forces about 9 km from Kramatorsk), inside Kostiantynivka where both sides hold parts of the city, and around Dobropillia where infiltrators have reached the centre. In the south, Ukrainian troops are pushing southeast of Oleksandrivka (Perebudova, Komar, Fedorivka reported retaken) and in southern Stepnohirsk, while Russia presses west of Huliaipole toward Orikhiv and stays more than 20 km from Zaporizhzhia city. Kupiansk is held by Ukraine, the Sumy and Kharkiv border 'security zone' offensives have taken only about 100 km2 each this year, and the Dnipro river line at Kherson is static apart from small boat raids. ISW counts a net Russian loss of 122 km2 since 1 September and says the fortress belt is unlikely to be taken militarily. A localised humanitarian ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky took effect at 03:00 Kyiv time on 27 October and runs to 1 November, and both sides were reported to be observing it; by 30 October it had held for 80 hours and evacuation convoys had left the town toward both Ukrainian-held territory and Russia. On 27 October Putin told the Finnish and Norwegian leaders that a deal must reflect 'realities on the ground' and NATO expansion. Trilateral talks are scheduled for 10 November in Abu Dhabi.
technical: Territory: ISW measured Russian gains at 13.2 km2 per day in 2025 but only 2.9 km2 per day in January to April 2026; by mid-October ISW counted about 100 km2 net for the whole of 2026 against Putin's claim of 6,500 km2.

Infiltration tactics: Russia now attacks mainly with small infiltration groups rather than mechanized columns; ISW repeatedly records Russian troops inside towns (Kostiantynivka, Dobropillia, Kupiansk) without consolidated positions, and flag-raising videos used for propaganda, some possibly AI-generated.
Kupiansk pipeline: Russian troops used a gas pipeline to infiltrate Kupiansk; Ukraine's Operation Veles took control of it and ISW links the end of Russian attacks there in October 2026 to that.
Starlink cutoff: in February 2026 Starlink blocked unregistered terminals used by Russian units, which degraded Russian command and control and helped open Ukraine's southern counteroffensive.

Drone branches: Russia formally created Unmanned Systems Forces on 12 November 2025 under Lt Col Yuri Vaganov, with the Rubikon Center as its elite unit and the 50th Varyag Brigade; Ukraine estimated 80,000 personnel in January and 114,000 in May 2026, with a target of about 165,000.

Rubikon: Russia's elite drone unit fought at Kostiantynivka and Lyman; ISW reported in October 2026 that Russia withdrew Rubikon operators from Lyman after heavy losses and sent the 50th Varyag Brigade instead.

Ukrainian Unmanned Systems Forces under Robert 'Madyar' Brovdi (since June 2025) include the 414th 'Birds of Madyar', 412th, 427th Rarog, 429th Achilles and 20th brigades; Ukraine claimed 33,000 Russian soldiers killed on video in December 2025 and 100,000 to 120,000 sorties a month.

Glide bombs: Zelensky said Russia used about 1,200 guided aerial bombs plus about 1,300 drones and dozens of ballistic missiles in a single week in mid-February 2026. Russia uses KAB-1500 glide bombs on rear cities (Sloviansk chemical plant hit 31 July 2026) and FAB-3000 bombs on river crossings such as the Oskil (October 2026).

Pace and cost: Russia's casualty cost per square mile rose from about 200 in 2025 to more than 9,600 in the first five months of 2026, using Ukrainian General Staff loss claims (Russia Matters via Mick Ryan).

Manpower: Russian recruitment ran about 940 per day against a target of 1,100 to 1,150 in mid-2026, and losses exceeded intake for four straight months from December 2025; ISW reported further recruitment decline in October 2026.
Armour: satellite imagery shows Russia refilling vehicle depots (Buy, Gagarka, Petrozavodsk, Topchikha) partly with refurbished vehicles; ISW judges the rebuild partial and modest.

Russian redeployments in October 2026 to stop the Ukrainian Oleksandrivka push: 120th Naval Infantry Division (Baltic Fleet), 40th Naval Infantry Brigade (Pacific Fleet) and 90th Tank Division (41st Combined Arms Army).

Order of battle around the fortress belt (ISW, October 2026): 25th CAA and Western Group at Lyman; 3rd CAA east of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk; 8th CAA at Kostiantynivka; 51st CAA (5th, 110th, 114th brigades) plus 61st Naval Infantry Brigade and 177th Naval Infantry Regiment at Dobropillia; Dnepr and Eastern groups at Orikhiv and Huliaipole.

Ukrainian units in key battles: 24th, 28th, 93rd and 129th Mechanized Brigades and 425th Skelya Regiment at Kostiantynivka; 53rd, 54th, 63rd Mechanized, 81st Airmobile, 117th and 120th Territorial Defence at Sloviansk; 7th Air Assault Corps, 82nd and 95th Air Assault Brigades, 1st Assault Regiment, 225th Assault Regiment and 37th Marine Brigade in the south.

Equipment attrition: Oryx had visually confirmed 24,236 Russian equipment losses since February 2022 (19,201 destroyed, 2,842 captured), including 4,451 tanks and 14,191 armoured combat vehicles, against 12,294 Ukrainian losses including 1,472 tanks and 6,147 armoured combat vehicles, as of its latest update (charts dated about 1 October 2026). These are photo-verified minimums, so real losses are higher.

North Korea: about 12 million artillery shells delivered by July 2025 (CFR estimate), 148 Hwasong-11 ballistic missiles by early 2025 (HUR), plus deminers and builders in Kursk; North Korean troops were still reported in Russian border regions in February 2026.
casualties: Russian military: BBC News Russian and Mediazona had identified 248,844 dead by name by 7 September 2026 and estimated 438,000 to 536,000 actually killed; Mediazona's count reached about 283,000 by 23 October 2026, including 7,920 officers. Western estimates: UK about 1.5 million Russian casualties including 500,000 killed (September 2026); CSIS about 1.4 million including 400,000 to 450,000 killed (July 2026). Ukrainian military: CSIS 525,000 to 625,000 casualties including 125,000 to 150,000 killed (July 2026); the UALosses project had named 96,821 dead and 97,938 missing by June 2026; Zelensky said 55,000 killed in early 2026, a figure widely seen as an undercount. Civilians: the UN verified at least 16,431 killed (803 children) and 48,613 injured by 30 June 2026 and says real numbers are higher; January to June 2026 saw 1,396 killed and 7,978 injured, up 37% on 2025, and September 2026 was worse still with 328 killed and 2,105 injured. All military figures are estimates with wide uncertainty.
displaced: UNHCR counted about 5.7 million Ukrainian refugees worldwide in September 2025, about 90% of them in Europe (Germany 1.2 million, Poland almost 1 million), and UNHCR and IOM put internally displaced people at about 5.3 million in 2024; no 2026 update was found in this research. Front-line evacuation continues: 44 settlements in Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia oblasts were ordered evacuated in January 2026, about 2,500 civilians remained in Kostiantynivka in April 2026, and about 90,000 of 440,000 prewar residents remained in Sloviansk and Kramatorsk in August 2026.

timeline.event: At least 250 Russian troops reported fighting inside Pokrovsk.
Battle of Kostiantynivka begins with Russian infiltration from the southeast.
Ukraine withdraws from Rivnopillia, opening the northern approach to Huliaipole; Russia announces its Unmanned Systems Forces are formed.
Russia claims capture of Pokrovsk; Ukraine denies it.
Berlin talks: US, Ukraine and Europe agree on a 'NATO-like' security guarantee in principle; territory unresolved.
Ukrainian General Staff confirms withdrawal from Siversk.
Russia claims Huliaipole; ISW confirms its capture in February 2026.
First US-Ukraine-Russia trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi end their second day without agreements; Russia insists on the 'Anchorage formula'.
Last evidence of Ukrainian troops in Pokrovsk; Myrnohrad assessed captured by this date.
Kremlin confirms it agreed to Trump's personal request not to strike Kyiv until 1 February.
Ukrainian counteroffensive opens on the Oleksandrivka front after Starlink cuts off Russian terminals.
Ukraine reports 'confident control' of Kupiansk, with a few dozen Russians left in one quarter.
Russian spring offensive against the Donetsk fortress belt opens (mid-March); March becomes Russia's costliest month at about 35,000 casualties.
Three-day Victory Day ceasefire (9 to 11 May) reduces but does not halt fighting.
Russian Defence Ministry claims full capture of Kostiantynivka; Ukraine rejects the claim the next day.
Zelensky says the southern counteroffensive has retaken 745 km2.
US envoys Witkoff and Kushner meet Putin in Moscow, then Zelensky in Kyiv on 6 September; no breakthrough.
Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps confirms Operation Vivaldi north of Lyman.
Putin rejects territorial concessions; ISW assesses Russia net lost 122 km2 since 1 September.
Ukrainian forces reportedly retake Perebudova, Komar and Fedorivka southeast of Oleksandrivka; Russian infiltrators reach central Dobropillia.
Oleshky humanitarian ceasefire takes effect until 1 November; Putin restates territorial and NATO demands in a call with Finland's Stubb and Norway's Store; ISW confirms no advances by either side.
Ukraine says the first 30 hours of the Oleshky ceasefire passed without incident; Kherson city reports no shelling for a day.
Oleshky ceasefire passes 80 hours intact; evacuation buses leave the town and split at Armiansk into convoys bound for Ukrainian-held territory and for Russia.

outlook: Watch Kostiantynivka and Dobropillia, the two places where Russia still has momentum, and whether Russian troops get within artillery-free range of Kramatorsk. Watch whether the Oleksandrivka counteroffensive reaches the Velyka Novosilka road junction that feeds Russia's push on Orikhiv. Winter will test Russia's recruitment, which is already below its losses, and Ukraine's dwindling Patriot interceptors as energy strikes intensify. The 10 November Abu Dhabi talks are the next diplomatic marker, but Moscow still demands territory it does not hold and rejects a ceasefire.

zones.name: Kostiantynivka and Druzhkivka
zones.note: Year-long urban battle; Russian 8th Combined Arms Army infiltrating the city, Ukrainian positions still held on the outskirts and in the west.

zones.name: Sloviansk and Kramatorsk eastern approaches
zones.note: Russian 3rd Combined Arms Army attacking toward Rai-Oleksandrivka, Mykolaivka, Kryva Luka and Malynivka; Russians about 9 to 10 km from the twin cities.

zones.name: Lyman and Operation Vivaldi
zones.note: Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps rolled back the Russian salient north of Lyman from September 2026.

zones.name: Siversk
zones.note: Fell to Russia in December 2025; now a Russian staging base for attacks west toward Sloviansk.

zones.name: Pokrovsk, Myrnohrad and Dobropillia
zones.note: Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad fell by January 2026; in October 2026 Russian infiltrators reached central Dobropillia.

zones.name: Oleksandrivka front (Ukrainian counteroffensive)
zones.note: Ukrainian Air Assault Forces counteroffensive since February 2026 along the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia oblast borders.

zones.name: Huliaipole to Orikhiv and Stepnohirsk
zones.note: Russian push west from Huliaipole toward Orikhiv; Ukrainian gains around Stepnohirsk in October 2026.

zones.name: Kupiansk and Borova (Oskil River)
zones.note: Ukraine retook Kupiansk by early 2026 and holds it; Russia keeps infiltrating and bombing Oskil crossings with FAB-3000s.

zones.name: Northern Kharkiv: Vovchansk and Velykyi Burluk
zones.note: Russian 'security zone' offensive along the border; about 115 km2 gained in 2026.

zones.name: Northern Sumy border
zones.note: Russian buffer-zone attacks; about 99 km2 gained in 2026.

zones.name: Kherson and the Dnipro river line
zones.note: Static river front; Russian boat raids on islands, heavy drone and glide-bomb attacks on Kherson city.

lines.name: Main contact line, Kharkiv border to Dnipro mouth (approximate, interpolated from ISW text descriptions)

battles.name: Battle for Dobropillia
sides: Russia: 51st Combined Arms Army (5th, 110th, 114th Motor Rifle Brigades), 61st Naval Infantry Brigade, 177th Naval Infantry Regiment
Ukraine: Dobropillia garrison
battles.outcome: Ongoing. Gerasimov claimed the town in mid-October; ISW saw only infiltration, but footage on 25 October shows Russian groups in the centre and Ukrainian logistics under drone interdiction.
battles.forces: Ukraine's General Staff logged 60 Russian attacks in this direction in one day (to 16 October 2026). Start date is when sources used here first record the assault on the town.
battles.significance: Dobropillia anchors the southwest of the fortress belt; Russia's Subordinate Main Effort 4 aims to envelop Kramatorsk from this side.

battles.name: Operation Vivaldi (Lyman counteroffensive)
battles.place: North of Lyman, Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine
sides: Ukraine: 3rd Army Corps (Andriy Biletsky)
Russia: 20th and 25th Combined Arms Armies, 1st Guards Tank Army, Western Group of Forces
battles.outcome: Ukrainian gains. Ukraine retook Novoselivka, Oleksandrivka, Yarova, Serednie, Shandryholove, Derylove and Drobysheve; ISW says the operation defeated Russia's plan to envelop the fortress belt from the northwest.
battles.forces: Ukraine reported 75 km2 in phase one and 40 km2 more in phase two (20 September); mappers estimated up to 240 km2. Russia sent the 50th Varyag drone brigade and withdrew Rubikon operators after heavy losses.
battles.losses: Ukraine claimed 800+ Russians killed in phase two and over 3,000 total Russian losses by 20 September (unverified).
battles.significance: Removed the northern pincer threatening Sloviansk and Kramatorsk and showed Ukraine can run corps-level offensives in 2026. Russia's claim on 19 September to have taken Lyman was contradicted by evidence.

battles.name: Orikhiv and Stepnohirsk fighting
sides: Russia: Dnepr and Eastern Groups of Forces
Ukraine: 17th Army Corps and Southern Defence Forces
battles.outcome: Ongoing. ISW counts 104.5 km2 and 8 settlements taken by Russia in Zaporizhzhia Oblast since 1 September 2026, but Ukraine holds Novoandriivka and has advanced in southern Stepnohirsk; Russians remain more than 20 km from Zaporizhzhia city.
battles.forces: Gerasimov claimed Russian troops were fighting in Orikhiv and 5 km from Zaporizhzhia city; ISW found both claims false. Ukraine denied street fighting in Orikhiv in April 2026.
battles.significance: Orikhiv is the hinge of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia line; a breakthrough here would expose Zaporizhzhia city, a regional capital of about 700,000 before the war.

battles.name: Russian advance on Sloviansk and Kramatorsk (Rai-Oleksandrivka and Mykolaivka)
battles.place: East of Sloviansk, Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine
sides: Russia: 3rd Combined Arms Army and Southern Group of Forces
Ukraine: 53rd, 54th, 63rd Mechanized, 81st Airmobile, 117th and 120th Territorial Defence Brigades
battles.outcome: Ongoing, slow Russian gains then stalemate. Russian units reached about 10 km from the twin cities by late July 2026 and fought for the Rai-Oleksandrivka heights; by October attacks near Kryva Luka and Malynivka were not advancing.
battles.forces: Start date approximates the mid-March 2026 opening of Russia's spring offensive on the fortress belt; coordinates are an approximate centre east of Sloviansk. A Russian tank assault on the southern approaches failed on 22 July 2026. KAB-1500 glide bombs hit the Sloviansk chemical plant on 31 July.
battles.significance: The northeast was Russia's most successful sector in 2026, but the Donets canal, dense fortifications and Ukraine's Vivaldi counteroffensive make an assault on the cities unlikely in 2026.

battles.name: 2026 Ukrainian counteroffensive (Oleksandrivka front)
battles.place: Oleksandrivka area, junction of Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia oblasts, Ukraine
sides: Ukraine: Air Assault Forces (7th Air Assault Corps, 82nd and 95th Air Assault Brigades), 1st Assault Regiment, 425th Skelya Regiment, 225th Assault Regiment, 37th Marine Brigade
Russia: 36th and 37th Motor Rifle Brigades, 14th Spetsnaz Brigade; later 120th Naval Infantry Division, 40th Naval Infantry Brigade, 90th Tank Division
battles.outcome: Ongoing Ukrainian success. Ukraine claimed 745 km2 and 26 villages by 12 August 2026; Russia retook Berezove, Ternove and Voskresenka; new Ukrainian gains reported at Perebudova, Komar and Fedorivka in October.
battles.forces: Launched after Starlink cut off Russian terminals in February 2026, which degraded Russian command and control. Coordinates are an approximate centre of the Oleksandrivka front.
battles.losses: Zelensky claimed 9,550 Russians killed and 6,600 wounded by 12 August 2026 (unverified). Ukrainian losses not published.
battles.significance: Ukraine's first monthly net territorial gain since the 2024 Kursk incursion and its largest gains since 2023; it largely halted Russia's spring-summer offensive in the south and forced Moscow to divert elite naval infantry.

battles.name: Russian 'security zone' offensive in Kharkiv and Sumy border areas
battles.place: Velykyi Burluk and Vovchansk areas, Kharkiv Oblast, and northern Sumy Oblast, Ukraine
sides: Russia: Northern Group of Forces (Col Gen Yevgeny Nikiforov)
Ukraine: border and Kharkiv defence units
battles.outcome: Limited Russian gains. ISW: 114.66 km2 net in Kharkiv Oblast and 99.1 km2 in Sumy Oblast since 1 January 2026; Russia controls only about 206 km2 of the claimed 600 km border strip.
battles.forces: Start date is the beginning of ISW's 2026 counting period, not a discrete opening. Coordinates mark Velykyi Burluk (approximate). Nikiforov claimed 75% of the border strip; Gerasimov claimed 461 km2 in northern Kharkiv. Ukrainian counterattacks near Starytsya in October 2026.
battles.significance: Putin calls the northern buffer zone non-negotiable, so Russian claims here shape its peace demands even though ISW calls the goal unattainable militarily.

battles.name: Battle of Kupiansk (2025-2026)
sides: Russia: Western Group of Forces infiltration units
Ukraine: Kupiansk garrison incl. Khartiia Brigade (National Guard) clearing forces
battles.outcome: Ukrainian victory. The Russian Defence Ministry claimed full capture on 20 November 2025; Zelensky visited the city on 12 December 2025 to disprove it; Ukraine raised its flag over city hall in early January 2026 and by 16 February only a few dozen Russians remained in one quarter, supplied by air drops.
battles.forces: Start date is the Russian capture claim; Russian troops had partially occupied the city since early October 2025. ISW put Russian strength in the city at about 100 to 200 troops in mid-December 2025 and Ukraine about 50 by late January 2026, supplied by drone. Russia had used a gas pipeline to infiltrate.
battles.significance: A rare reversal of a Russian capture claim, it exposed false reporting by Russian generals and kept the Oskil River line in Ukrainian hands.

battles.name: Battle of Kostiantynivka
sides: Russia: 8th Combined Arms Army incl. 70th Motor Rifle Division, 4th and 72nd Motor Rifle Brigades, Rubikon Center
Ukraine: 24th, 28th, 93rd and 129th Mechanized Brigades, 425th Skelya Regiment
battles.outcome: Ongoing and contested. Russia claimed capture on 3 July 2026; in late October Ukraine still holds positions on the southern outskirts and in the west while Russian groups infiltrate the north.
battles.forces: Russian infiltration from the southeast and southwest reached the zinc plant (March 2026) and metallurgical plant and Kryvyi Torets river (June); Ukrainian commanders counted up to 250 Russians inside the city in June and 145 in July.
battles.losses: Zelensky claimed on 23 August 2026 that 70 to 80% of Russia's 267,000 losses in 2026 were in this direction (unverified). Civilians: about 2,500 remained in April 2026.
battles.significance: The southern gate to the Donetsk fortress belt and the war's main meat-grinder of 2026; a premature Russian victory claim that still has not come true a year in.

battles.name: Fall of Pokrovsk (final phase of the Pokrovsk offensive)
sides: Russia: Central Group of Forces
Ukraine: 7th Air Assault Corps and attached brigades
battles.outcome: Russian victory. Russia claimed the city on 1 December 2025; no Ukrainian presence after 28 January 2026; ISW confirmed full Russian control in late February 2026.
battles.forces: Ukraine's 7th Corps estimated about 11,000 Russian troops in the area in late October 2025. Russian infiltration groups of a few hundred worked into the city from the south and west.
battles.losses: No reliable totals. Ukrainian claims through 2024 and 2025 spoke of hundreds of Russian casualties per day in this direction. Ukrainian losses not published.
battles.significance: Pokrovsk was a road and rail hub and Ukraine's main coking-coal source. It took Russia about 18 months from the first approach, and ISW noted Russia could not exploit the capture, which helped stall its 2026 advance.

sides: Russia: Central Group of Forces
Ukraine: units defending the Pokrovsk-Myrnohrad agglomeration
battles.outcome: Russian victory. ISW assessed Russia captured Myrnohrad before 28 January 2026 and Russian command posts moved in.
battles.forces: Russia claimed Balahan east of the town on 14 October 2025 and pressed the pocket from north and south.
battles.significance: Closing the twin-city pocket ended the Pokrovsk battle and freed Russian units to push north toward Dobropillia and Rodynske.

battles.name: Huliaipole offensive
sides: Russia: 36th and 37th Motor Rifle Brigades (Eastern Group of Forces)
Ukraine: 141st Mechanized Brigade, 102nd and 106th Territorial Defence Brigades, 225th Assault Battalion
battles.outcome: Russian victory. Russia claimed Huliaipole on 27 December 2025; ISW confirmed its capture in its 6 February 2026 assessment.
battles.forces: Russia crossed the Yanchur river in late October, took Rivnopillia (Ukraine withdrew 12 November) and entered the town from the north and east in December.
battles.losses: Ukrainian Southern Defence Forces claimed about 250 Russian soldiers and 50 pieces of equipment destroyed per day in late November 2025 (unverified).
battles.significance: Huliaipole had been static since 2022 and Ukrainian defences faced south, so the attack from the east threatened to outflank the Zaporizhzhia line and triggered Ukraine's February counteroffensive.

battles.name: Battle of Siversk
sides: Russia: Southern Group of Forces (3rd Combined Arms Army)
Ukraine: Siversk garrison
battles.outcome: Russian victory. Gerasimov claimed the town on 11 December 2025; ISW judged it taken by 21 December; Ukraine confirmed withdrawal on 23 December.
battles.forces: Start date approximates the September to October 2025 approach. Russian forces closed in from north, east and south through the Serebriansky forest, putting the Lyman road under fire control.
battles.significance: Ended a front that had held since 2022 and gave Russia a staging base 31 km east of Sloviansk for its 2026 push on the fortress belt.
